text:
Bitcoin reclaimed the $63,100–$63,500 range on Monday, July 6, hitting an intraday peak of $63,882 as U.S. markets reopened after the long holiday weekend. Dovish sentiment from Thursday’s weak 57K payroll print continues to support risk-on assets, dragging the 10-year Treasury yield down to 4.46%. While geopolitical tensions in the Strait of Hormuz kept the DXY resilient near 101.00, equity futures signaled a tech-led positive start to the week as the Q2 earnings season kicks off.

Institutional sentiment remains cautiously constructive, stabilized by the $221.7 million ETF inflow turn. A new valuation framework released by Salomon Brothers today further supported the positive sentiment, linking Bitcoin’s long-term value to USD money supply (M2) expansion. Investors now look to Wednesday’s FOMC minutes to confirm the Fed’s data-dependent easing path under Kevin Warsh.
